source.title: The Tolman-Eichenbaum Machine: Unifying Space and Relational Memory through Generalization in the Hippocampal Formation.

confidence_rationale: A model built entirely on pairwise transition structure reproduces the diversity of entorhinal and hippocampal cell types, matches non-spatial relational task recordings, and yields a confirmed novel prediction (structure preserved across remapping) -- all without any representation above a pairwise relation. That is a substantive existence proof against Q-084's necessity claim. Held at 0.68 because absence of a need in one model family is not absence of a need in general, and TEM was never tested against the multistep typed-path readouts Q-084 specifies.
failure_signatures: A purely pairwise-transition model accounts for grid, band, border, object-vector, place and landmark cells plus non-spatial relational task representations, so the observed richness of hippocampal-entorhinal coding is not by itself evidence that higher-order structure is represented.

TEM's generalisation comes from factorising structure from sensory content, not from higher-order relations -- so an REE metapath readout that beats a pairwise baseline might be recovering factorisation the pairwise baseline failed to learn, rather than genuinely higher-order information.
The model was never compared against a metapath-aware or hyperedge readout, so its success bounds the necessity claim without testing the sufficiency claim Q-084 poses.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Medial entorhinal cells form a basis describing structural knowledge and hippocampal cells bind that basis to sensory representations; a model built on this principle (TEM), learning from sequences of pairwise transitions, reproduces grid, band, border, object-vector, place and landmark cell types, matches representations recorded in complex non-spatial tasks, and correctly predicts that structural knowledge is preserved across hippocampal remapping.
mapping.ree_translation: Q-084 asks whether higher-order relational structure is REQUIRED. TEM is the strongest available counterexample: it is built from pairwise transition structure alone, contains nothing resembling a hyperedge or metapath, and nonetheless captures the phenomena Q-084's motivating examples appeal to -- multistep functional roles emerging from relational position. For REE this says that a pairwise typed-edge topology (MECH-468 projection F) with the right factorisation of structure from content may already exhaust what a metapath-aware readout would add, and that Q-084's probe must therefore control for factorisation quality, not just for path length.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This weakens the NECESSITY claim without answering the comparison Q-084 actually specifies: TEM was never benchmarked against a metapath-aware or hyperedge readout on the same held-out functional labels, so its success shows higher-order structure was not needed FOR TEM'S TASKS, not that it is never needed. The tasks are also mostly graph-traversal and relational-inference problems with homogeneous edge semantics, whereas Q-084's motivating cases are heterogeneous TYPED paths (hazard, repair opportunity, goal completion). And TEM is a model of biology, not biology -- its success constrains what is sufficient to reproduce recordings, which is weaker than constraining what the brain does.
mapping.source_context: Computational model (TEM) trained on structured sequence prediction, compared against rodent entorhinal/hippocampal recordings including simultaneously recorded place and grid cells across remapping, and against non-spatial relational task data.

confidence_components.notes: Very high source quality -- Cell, model plus confirmed novel empirical prediction. Mapping fidelity moderate: it is a clean existence proof against necessity but does not run Q-084's specified comparison. Transfer risk relatively low because TEM is itself a computational agent architecture, so the REE mapping is unusually direct for a neuroscience entry.
